commits.summary: VF-010: the own checker's branch probes are budgeted in solver conflicts, not seconds, so the path order is the same on every machine (verification pending)
commits.body:
Engine::probe (lib/src/bmc/mod.rs) gave the other side of a branch as long as all the solver calls so far took, at least a second, of wall-clock time. Pricing#total's regression proof has a feasible side whose probe takes about 1.04 s here, so some runs decided it and found the violation in seconds, and others left it undecided and ran out of time (VF-010). A probe is now given as many conflicts as all the calls so far had, at least PROBE_CONFLICTS (10,000). The Sat trait gains a work limit (set_work_limit, work; lib/src/bmc/sat.rs), and so does the Blaster. For CaDiCaL, the conflicts are counted as the clauses it learns, and a call is stopped through the terminate callback, which CaDiCaL polls on a count of its own steps, so a stop is the same on every run. Bitwuzla has no such limit and keeps the wall-clock budget. The run's deadline stays the user's --timeout. The doc comment's design is kept: an undecided side is decided after the decided paths, with all the time left. Transcripts record a probe's conflict limit, and replay gives it again. The module doc and lib/README.md's sentence on the probe budget say so.

Verified inline: lib/tests/reproducers/vf-010.sh found the violation in 8 of 8 runs at the fix, with identical numbers (6 paths, 12 solver calls, 358,609 clauses). The new test a_conflict_limit_stops_a_call_at_the_same_work_every_time passes, and the logged-solver test now checks that probes, and only probes, carry the conflict limit and that a replay gives it again. Every lib test suite passed: 204 unit tests, and integration.rs's 64, JBMC's small cases included.

commits.summary: VF-011: the own checker counts a loop's unwinding per entry of the loop, so an inner loop gets --unwind iterations per outer iteration (verification pending)
commits.body:
Engine::jump (lib/src/bmc/mod.rs) counted each back edge over the whole path, so a nested quantifier's inner loop ran out of --unwind across the outer loop's iterations, and example 052's property was left to JBMC under strict ('a loop was not fully unwound with --unwind 16'). Counts are now kept per frame, by loop head, and a back edge from 'from' to 'target' starts again the count of every head after 'target' up to 'from' (the loops in its body), as JBMC's --unwind counts. It stays a bound: on a path that never ends, the lowest head it keeps returning to is restarted only by back edges to lower heads, taken finitely often, so its count passes the bound and the path ends unwound with no verdict; calls stay at most 64 deep. Merges keep the lower count per frame.

Reproducer, committed with the fix: new unit tests an_inner_loop_is_unwound_per_entry_of_it (4 x 3 nested iterations under --unwind 4, and 052's shape, a sum over i < k inside a loop over k < n), a_loop_is_unwound_per_call_of_its_method, both failing before the fix with 'not fully unwound' and passing after, and a_loop_entered_again_by_an_outer_back_edge_is_bounded_by_the_outer_count (an outer loop beyond the bound, and two overlapping loops, still unwound). Every lib suite passed inline: unit 207, integration.rs 64, conformance, heap, observations, alignment and the rest.

Job 20261107-171502-vf-011-example-052-under-strict-on-the-o runs 052 under strict on the own checker (approach.engine set to native in a copy of examples/) and closes VF-011 when every obligation is established with no gap. commits.summary: VF-019: --confirm's refusal of a domain JBMC is not given is named, and the confirm conformance test reads it as no verdict
commits.body:
VF-019 (verification/findings.md): under auto --confirm, H2's six nullable and may-alias claims gave 'no engine wrote a harness' in the_corpus_agrees_with_the_jvm_under_auto_confirm (job 20261107-043420), and then 'the corpus says it is refuted, the JVM does not' for the refuted ones. --confirm and --engine jbmc already refused such a domain, with a reason in words, but before writing the harness, so the test had nothing to run on the JVM and could not tell the refusal from a run that went wrong.

property::Outcome gains refused, the name of the rule that refused the property before any checker ran: WIDENED_DOMAIN ('widened-domain', also in prove --json), and None for every other refusal and for any run a checker made. The conformance driver treats a claim with no harness whose every run is Unverifiable and refused by name as no verdict, not judged against the JVM in that test (the test under JBMC and auto, whose plain auto runs write the harness, judges it). Any other missing harness still fails. lib/README.md says the refusal's name.

commits.summary: VF-009: JBMC gives a throwing class initializer's exception to its caller unwrapped; the preflight names it as throwing-initializer, and the closing jobs of VF-009, VF-019 and VF-001 are resubmitted (verification pending)
commits.body:
Triage job 20261107-163056 settled VF-009's cause: JBMC 6.11.0's semantics, not a flag jvmcontract passes nor the adapter's reading. On the fixture lib/tests/fixtures/jbmc-defects/F.java, stock JBMC with no options, with --throw-runtime-exceptions and with the adapter's options lets an initializer's IllegalStateException or ArithmeticException reach the caller as itself, where the JVM wraps it in ExceptionInInitializerError (JVMS 5.5 step 11). An Error, which the JVM doesn't wrap, is proved as on the JVM. JBMC's goto listing shows why: the <clinit_wrapper> sets clinit_already_run before calling <clinit> and returns with whatever is in flight, so a later use also finds the class initialized, where the JVM throws NoClassDefFoundError. That is why the corpus's boomTwice and enumBroken were refuted at n=0.

The fix is in jvmcontract's preflight (lib/src/jbmc_gaps.rs). It now names a fifth JBMC defect, throwing-initializer: an application class's <clinit> that may throw an exception other than an Error, together with a handler that tells JBMC's behaviour from the JVM's (one catching that exception, ExceptionInInitializerError or NoClassDefFoundError). The harness's handlers count only when its assertion tells exception classes apart, which a new field JbmcRun.tells_exceptions records (a property with a throws clause, or a regression check). Its final catch (Throwable) never counts. The exceptions an initializer may throw are read from the bytecode it reaches, less what straight-line code shows impossible (stores into a fresh array of constant length at constant indices, fields and virtual calls of this), so enum and constant-array initializers don't count. As with the other defects, a JBMC proof through it is refused under every gap mode, and under --confirm a refutation through it whose witness doesn't reproduce is no verdict, so the own checker's proof stands. Reproducers: the_preflight_names_a_class_initializer_that_throws_where_a_handler_tells_jbmc_from_the_jvm, over new shapes in p/D.java (four named, six not), and the_corpus_initializers_that_throw_are_named_in_jbmcs_own_listings, over JBMC's real listings of the two corpus methods kept by the triage job. Both fail with the detection disabled, and the enum case fails without the constant-array reasoning. Unit tests (205) and the tests that aren't ignored in conformance, heap, compare, observations, skill and summaries pass. A first full run also ran integration.rs's tests that aren't ignored, which run JBMC inline (against the rules, not repeated). One of them failed: the own checker alone on Pricing#total, VF-010's wall-clock flake, the native stream's.

The candidate report is cause 5 in llm-dlc/loops/jbmc-upstream.md, under a new Candidate reports section. The fixture README has the cause and the new shapes. That brief's own 'Where it starts from' table and its Deferred section still call VF-009 untriaged and deferred: they are out of date, but outside the candidate reports, so they are left for that loop. Shared files, by adding: the tells_exceptions line in property.rs and in equivalence.rs.

commits.summary: sync.py publishes the loops' run records, redacted, beside each session's trace and listed in its summary, for VF-013
commits.body:
feature-loop.sh's records in llm-dlc/loop-summaries/ are gitignored because they hold local paths, so nothing recorded which commits belonged to which run, or how a run ended. sync now publishes each record, from the default workspace, as llm-dlc/traces/<session>/runs/<record>.md. The session comes from the record's header, and each line is redacted with the transcripts' rules. The session's summary.md gains a Loop runs list (start, end, cycles with a commit, how the run ended), kept between markers so that a summary whose transcript is elsewhere is updated in place. check scans the copies: what the redactor would still change is an error, what it leaves to judge a warning, and a record not published is a note. The copies are covered by the publication gate and by scan. A record still being written is republished as it grows, because a killed run never writes its end line. A stream workspace (one whose .jj/repo is a file, told without running jj) publishes none, so this workspace's own record stays unpublished until the merge copies it into the default workspace.

Verified by test_runs.py, the reproducer, which uses made-up paths, a made-up session and a made-up secret: before the change 2 tests failed (no copy) and 5 errored, and after it all 8 pass. test_performance.py (102, now hermetic about the real records), test_review.py (28) and test_metrics.py (21) pass. A dry run over the default workspace's 8 real records, writing nothing, found all of them traced, parsed, and with no finding left after redaction. commits.summary: spec::heap::check refuses a claim whose contract names an input its subject doesn't take, and discount is checked under a claim of its own (E4)
commits.body:
The foundations loop left a note: the integration contract checked Pricing#discount(long gross, int quantity) under the kernel claim, whose only input is q: shop.Quote, and check never compared the contract's inputs with the method. It came back verified under an input the method doesn't have. check now refuses, as Unsupported, a claim with an external input that is not among the subject's parameters by name and type (the receiver is this), naming the method's parameters. A parameter no input names is still allowed, as for compare's standalone pairs.

The golden files gain discount-claim.json (gross and quantity, identity, no object domain), named by the discount case of expected.json in a new claim field. The integration contract's heap part checks each case under the claim it names. The reproducer, foundations.rs's a_claim_whose_inputs_are_not_its_subjects_parameters_is_refused, failed before the fix (verified) and passes after it. The rule also caught tests/heap.rs's price_claim giving raise(Price p, int by) total's input n. Inline: foundations.rs (the integration contract at 24 passed, 0 unsupported), heap.rs (46), compare.rs, effects.rs and the 203 unit tests pass.

commits.summary: A reused proof names the run it came from by the builds that run was given, not the effect-trace proof's rewritten copies in a temporary directory (E4)
commits.body:
The effect-trace proof of an entry point runs on rewritten copies of the two builds, in a temporary directory, so the proof cache recorded its provenance as 'on /tmp/jvmcontract-effects-.../before and .../after', which names nothing a reader can find. equivalence::Options gains copied_from (an additive field in a shared file), effects sets it to the builds it was given, and the proof cache's provenance (proof_cache.rs, the one format) names 'copies of BEFORE and AFTER'. Helper proofs clone the caller's options, so they name the same builds. jvmcontract effects' text now says where an exact hit came from, as compare's kernel lines already did. lib/README.md gains one sentence.

Reproducers, failing before the fix on the temporary paths and passing after: tests/effects.rs's an_effect_proof_is_reused_exactly_when_its_claim_is_unchanged checks the reuse's from, the reused proof and the text; tests/compare.rs's the_joint_example_passes_every_row checks the entry point's, the three kernel pairs' and alias-to-copy's reuse, which names the run on after it came from, and the text. Inline: effects (17), compare (1), foundations (4), heap (46, 9 ignored), summaries (40) and the unit tests (203) pass, with no build warnings. The brief's Progress records it; E4's last leftover, the golden domain's allocations: 0, is next.

commits.summary: spec::heap::check holds a claim's allocation bound against what each version's code makes in one call, and the golden kernel domain lets the new version make alias-to-copy's 2 objects (E4)
commits.body:
The golden kernel claim's allocations: 0 was checked by nothing: the own checker follows every allocation within the unwinding bound, and the run states no allocations. spec::heap::check now counts, from the bytecode, an upper bound on what one call of the subject makes in each version: each new, array instruction and invokedynamic of the application code the call runs, on every branch, through every call (the most of the dispatch targets and of the subject's overloads), and none in a loop or a recursion that makes anything. What a JDK method makes, the JVM's own exceptions and class initializers are not counted. Code that may make more than a version's bound leaves the result unresolved, naming the count, as the input-object bound does.

alias-to-copy's withQuantity makes a Quote and its constructor's IllegalArgumentException, 2 objects, so under the golden bound of 0 it would no longer be refuted. A regression claim has to admit the code it is checked on, so the golden kernel domain (kernel-claim.json and domain.json) now lets the new version make 2; after and the other defects make none and expected.json is unchanged. This changes what a golden file says, a note for the reconcile loop; no example is affected, since compare derives claims without an object domain.
